newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin confident before heart surgery - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin confident before heart surgery - Kremlin.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, confident that he would soon be back at work, said in a statement released before the start of Tuesday's heart operation that he was sure things would go well and there would be no power vacuum.
"I am sure everything will go alright," said the statement, read out by spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky at a news conference. "I believe that I will soon be working at full strength, as I did before."
Yeltsin, thanking Russians for their letters and telegrams of support, reassured his fellow citizens that there would be no power vacuum when he was under the anaesthetic.
He said power had been transferred to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, and a tried and tested team was running Russia.
"The country will not be without a leader for a minute," Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin's appeal to the nation as saying.

Yeltsin, 65, said in September he would have an operation on his heart and doctors have been preparing for the surgery since then. They said last week they had overcome a series of complicating factors, including anaemia and thyroid problems.

Yastrzhembsky said a team of four surgeons, headed by Russian specialist Renat Akchurin, had started operating on Yeltsin at 7 a.m. (0400 GMT). Surgery of this kind usually lasted six to eight hours, he added.
Foreign doctors are advising the Russian medical team, but Yastrzhembsky said they were not due in the hospital until well into the operation.
Russian officials have made clear that the foreigners, who include U.S. pioneering heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, will not wield the surgeon's knife.

Yastrzhembsky said the president was in jovial mood before the operation, joking with chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov. "Are you here with the knife already?" Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as asking Mironov.
